item.title: [Recap] Cam Spencer (MEM): Cam Spencer amassed nine points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, six assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:
Cam Spencer amassed nine points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), five rebounds, six assists and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.

While Ty Jerome’s return from a hip injury meant Spencer resumed his usual backup duties, his playing time was unaffected. With Javon Small (personal) away from the team, Spencer still played 30 minutes and provided solid value in assists. Rostered in 47 percent of Yahoo leagues, the third-year guard has been close to a top-100 player in nine-cat formats. He’s worth holding onto, even with Jerome’s return.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jahmai Mashack (MEM): Jahmai Mashack recorded zero points (0-of-1 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:
Jahmai Mashack recorded zero points (0-of-1 FGs), two rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.

Mashack wasn’t on the fantasy radar before Saturday’s game, and his lack of production certainly didn’t change that. He started for Cameron Boozer, who was sidelined with a sprained right ankle, and played 22 minutes. Mashack could get another start against the Hornets on Monday if Boozer remains out, but there’s no need to consider rostering him in redraft leagues.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Cedric Coward (MEM): Cedric Coward finished Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 23 points (8-of-16 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and four three-pointers.
item.description:
Cedric Coward finished Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves with 23 points (8-of-16 FGs, 3-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals and four three-pointers.

Coward led the Grizzlies in scoring on Saturday, shooting 50 percent from the field. However, he also committed a game-high six turnovers, the most he’s had in an NBA game. In addition to his points, the rebounds, steals and three-pointers should help offset the high turnover count for fantasy managers.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Ty Jerome (MEM): Ty Jerome (hip) tallied 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
item.description:
Ty Jerome (hip) tallied 18 points (7-of-17 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), four rebounds, six assists, two steals and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Timberwolves.

Back in the Grizzlies’ lineup after a four-game absence, Jerome showed some signs of rust on Saturday. However, to say that was the lone reason for his five-turnover night would be unfair to the Timberwolves, who have one of the best collections of perimeter defenders in the NBA. This wasn’t Jerome’s best night, but his ability to play 27 minutes without aggravating the hip injury is a positive going into Week 6. Memphis plays four games next week, starting with the Hornets on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] LaMelo Ball (MIN): LaMelo Ball notched 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
item.description:
LaMelo Ball notched 12 points (5-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.

With Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu and Jonathan Kuminga (16/4/2 with one block and two three-pointers) all scoring at least 16 points, Ball took a step back scoring-wise on Saturday. After an inefficient shooting night against the Knicks on Thursday, the Timberwolves’ point guard made 50 percent of his attempts against the Grizzlies. Even better for fantasy managers was that Ball recorded a full stat line, his second of the season and the first since a November 4 win over the Rockets. Minnesota plays four games next week, starting with the Nets on Monday.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Jaden McDaniels (MIN): Jaden McDaniels accounted for 25 points (11-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Jaden McDaniels accounted for 25 points (11-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), five rebounds, four assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.

A double-digit scorer in all 17 games he’s played this season, McDaniels scored a season-high 25 points on Saturday. The Timberwolves forward, already one of the NBA’s top on-ball defenders, is enjoying his most productive offensive season. McDaniels is averaging career highs in points, rebounds, assists and three-pointers. Given the ADP of 85, he may be one of the early steals of the season in fantasy basketball.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Ayo Dosunmu (MIN): Ayo Dosunmu recorded 19 points (9-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.
item.description:
Ayo Dosunmu recorded 19 points (9-of-14 FGs), two rebounds, two assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Grizzlies.

After scoring at least 18 points in each of Minnesota’s first six games of November, Dosunmu has run “hot and cold” recently. Limited to six points in Thursday’s loss to the Knicks, he rebounded nicely on Saturday. Even with the recent run of inconsistent scoring, Dosunmu has been a top-50 fantasy player over the last month. With Anthony Edwards (knee) not having a return timeline, Dosunmu is well-positioned to provide reliable fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kyrie Irving (DAL): Kyrie Irving amassed 25 points (8-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and four assists over 35 minutes to lift the Mavericks to a 110-100 victory over the Clippers.
item.description:
Kyrie Irving amassed 25 points (8-of-24 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), six rebounds and four assists over 35 minutes to lift the Mavericks to a 110-100 victory over the Clippers.

Irving got off to a sluggish start by his lofty standards but he responded with a 16-point performance in the second half to help Dallas pull away for good. The 34-year-old point guard hasn’t skipped a beat in his return from last year’s knee surgery, averaging 22.5 points, 3.8 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.2 steals through 13 games this season. The Mavericks close out the week with a road tilt against the Jazz on Sunday.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Brook Lopez (LAC): Brook Lopez delivered a team-high 21 points (8-of-15 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds and one block over 25 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Mavericks.
item.description:
Brook Lopez delivered a team-high 21 points (8-of-15 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), six rebounds and one block over 25 minutes in Saturday’s loss to the Mavericks.

Lopez has been an unexpected impact fantasy contributor during his age-38 campaign, scoring 20 points or more in three consecutive games and six of his last eight overall since November 4. He’s taken advantage of his opportunity to play a larger role on the rebuilding Clippers following their turbulent offseason and figures to be on the move to a contender at the upcoming trade deadline. He should be rostered in all fantasy leagues at this juncture. The Clippers have a busy four-game week upcoming with showdowns against the Rockets, Grizzlies, Pelicans and Warriors on tap.

George Bissell

item.title: [Recap] Jabari Smith (HOU): Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Friday.
item.description:
Jabari Smith Jr. finished with 21 points (7-of-8 FGs), four rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Friday.

Following a hot start to the season, Smith has cooled down a bit in the month of November. This was his first time scoring at least 20 points in a game since Oct. 31, and he only did it because he was insanely efficient. Hopefully, his volume will start to tick back up so he can get back to being elite for fantasy managers, as he was in October. He’ll look to carry this production into their next matchup with the Clippers on Monday.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Fred VanVleet (HOU): Fred VanVleet lit up the Nuggets with 25 points (10-of-21 FGs), one rebound, nine assists, one steal and three three-pointers on Friday.
item.description:
Fred VanVleet lit up the Nuggets with 25 points (10-of-21 FGs), one rebound, nine assists, one steal and three three-pointers on Friday.

Despite missing all of last season, VanVleet has still been solid in fantasy basketball so far this year. He was able to set a new season high for scoring in this game, making this the first time he scored at least 25 points in a game since March of 2025. VanVleet’s presence in the lineup has been huge for Houston this year, and he proved in this game that he’s still capable of big scoring nights, even if they aren’t going to come consistently.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić put up 25 points (9-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and six turnovers in the 106-104 win over the Kings.
item.description:
Luka Dončić put up 25 points (9-of-18 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and six turnovers in the 106-104 win over the Kings.

Luka continues to dominate the game and the Kings couldn’t do much to stop him. In the clutch, Keegan Murray did get a steal on him which could’ve cost the Lakers the game. You would wish the turnover numbers go down, but with the load that he’s had to do on offense, it’s hard to complain too much. He’s dominating everyone else from a statistical basis that is helping you in other areas.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Alperen Şengün (HOU): Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-16 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 133-124 loss to the Nuggets on Friday.
item.description:
Alperen Şengün led the Rockets with 28 points (9-of-16 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), 11 rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in a 133-124 loss to the Nuggets on Friday.

Şengün recorded his second triple-double of the season, but it wasn’t enough for Houston to secure the win. It has been a fantastic season for Şengün so far, as he is currently averaging career highs in points, assists, three-pointers and free throw percentage. He has been on the cusp of this type of production over the last few seasons, and it seems like he’s finally reaching it. The Rockets have started the season well, and Şengün has been right at the center of it.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Christian Braun (DEN): Christian Braun lit up the Rockets with 19 points (7-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 133-124 win on Friday.
item.description:
Christian Braun lit up the Rockets with 19 points (7-of-10 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, four steals, one block and three three-pointers in a 133-124 win on Friday.

Last year was a down one for Braun, but he has bounced back to start this season. The offense is starting to pick up, but it’s his defensive impact that has been the biggest difference. He has at least one steal in every game this season and has had two or more in 10 of his 14 games, which has led to his career-high 2.3 steals per game. That’s carrying his category league value right now, which means he’s mostly been a one-trick pony, though he has been decent in a few other categories.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes got himself 13 points (2-of-7 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, and a three in the win over the Kings on Friday.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes got himself 13 points (2-of-7 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), five rebounds, seven assists, and a three in the win over the Kings on Friday.

Grimes started off slowly but got going later in the game and helped the Lakers hold on. He’s still worth holding, but coach JJ Reddick did say that he’s hoping to have Austin Reaves back on Monday against the Jazz, or on Friday against the San Antonio Spurs. So sell high if you can, or ride it out and drop when Reaves comes back.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Cameron Johnson (DEN): Cameron Johnson finished with 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday.
item.description:
Cameron Johnson finished with 19 points (7-of-13 FGs), three rebounds, six assists, two steals and two three-pointers against the Rockets on Friday.

It has been another rough season in Denver for Johnson, but this was one of his best performances of the season, which included a new season high for assists. Johnson had a strong final season in Brooklyn, but he hasn’t been able to achieve that level of production during his two seasons as a Nugget. However, if he is able to provide lines like this, especially on a quieter night from Jamal Murray, Denver and fantasy managers will both be happy.

Noah Rubin

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler put up 15 points (7-of-11 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three blocks, and a three in the win over the Kings.
item.description:
Walker Kessler put up 15 points (7-of-11 FGs, 0-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, a steal, and three blocks, and a three in the win over the Kings.

Kessler had a very good game despite being in foul trouble. He had his way with Sabonis being in the paint and put up some good numbers. The two free throws he missed where in the clutch to ice the game. He hit a three in this game which was the first of the season. However, it’s a good performance all things considered.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] DeMar DeRozan (DEN): DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.
item.description:
DeMar DeRozan provided a boost off the bench with 15 points (4-of-11 FGs), two rebounds, two assists and one steal against the Rockets on Friday.

DeRozan started this season scoring in double figures in each of Denver’s first three games. In the 10 games since, he has only scored in double figures three more times. The positive news is that he’s reached that mark in back-to-back games. DeRozan isn’t going to provide value anywhere near what he has throughout his career, but if he can continue to be a reliable bench scorer for Denver, he’ll be a valuable piece for this team when the playoffs arrive.

Noah Rubin

Edwards underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee in October, and it was reported that he could be out for over two months. When asked about his recovery progress, Edwards said that he was unsure when he’d be able to play again. He hoped to avoid needing surgery, but that became unavoidable once the knee flared up after the regular season began. “It was good in [training] camp, like I said,” Edwards said. “I think after the Miami game it started to flare up, and then it went down a little bit after the Orlando game, so we thought we were going to be alright, but then after the back-to-back it was really bad, like painful to fly, so I’m like, ‘I gotta get it.” Ayo Dosunmu has been the starter with Edwards out and should be rostered in most fantasy leagues until that changes.

item.title: [Recap] Walker Kessler (LAL): Walker Kessler had a stat line of 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, and an assist against his former team, the Jazz on Wednesday.
item.description:
Walker Kessler had a stat line of 10 points (3-of-7 FGs, 4-of-10 FTs), 11 rebounds, and an assist against his former team, the Jazz on Wednesday.

Walker Kessler had a good performance except for the free throw percentage where he went 4-of-10. There might be a slight buy low opportunity here for Walker if someone is mad about the FT% and the lack of scoring that he’s had over the past few games. He should bounce back, but he’s not the player that people saw in the first two games of the season where he looked amazing.

item.title: [Recap] Quentin Grimes (LAL): Quentin Grimes got 20 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, and four 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday to Jazz.
item.description:
Quentin Grimes got 20 points (8-of-20 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, and four 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday to Jazz.

Grimes continued his run after an insane game against the Hornets on Tuesday. He’s been the big beneficiary of the Reaves injury at this point. He’s wroth having until Reaves comes back, but once he does, he’s a streamer for points and 3’s only. The usage won’t be the same as it was during this run. This is a sell high if you have him on your roster currently.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Luka Dončić (LAL): Luka Dončić scored 29 points (10-of-28 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), got five rebounds, seven assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and 9 turnovers in 109-97 loss to Jazz.
item.description:
Luka Dončić scored 29 points (10-of-28 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), got five rebounds, seven assists, two steals, two 3-pointers, and 9 turnovers in 109-97 loss to Jazz.

The run that Luka is on this season is incredible. You can pencil him in for a great game every night and there’s nothing the opponent can do about it. It wasn’t even the best night and he still produced. You wish the turnovers are lower, but he’s having to do everything for this team, especially with Austin Reaves out of the lineup.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Ace Bailey (UTA): Ace Bailey got himself 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, a steal, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.
item.description:
Ace Bailey got himself 19 points (7-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, a steal, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday.

Ace has been more inconsistent as of late with his shooting, but the Jazz needed offense with Darryn being in foul trouble, and Ace at least put up shots and impacted the game in other ways defensively. There might be a bit of a buy low still with the efficiency, especially with the 3PT shooting being as low as it is, but he’s been great this year for the Jazz.

Brian Taylor

item.title: [Recap] Svi Mykhailiuk (UTA): Svi Mykhailiuk put up 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.
item.description:
Svi Mykhailiuk put up 15 points (4-of-10 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and four 3-pointers in win on Wednesday.

It’s been a terrible start to the season for Svi. He wasn’t going to continue to shoot as poorly as he has, so it’s nice to see a decent bounce back game from him. He’s only a player for deeper leagues as a streamer, but it’s good to commend him for his performance tonight since he played 34 minutes with Darryn Peterson getting into foul trouble.

item.title: [Recap] Keyonte George (UTA): Keyonte Geroge scores 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and five 3-pointers in the 109-97 win over the Lakers.
item.description:
Keyonte Geroge scores 30 points (9-of-17 FGs, 7-of-9 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and five 3-pointers in the 109-97 win over the Lakers.

George was carrying the offense for the Jazz and keeping them in the first half of this game. Darryn Peterson was having foul trouble, so it was on him to keep the Jazz in the game. He helped lead them to get the win in this one. It’s been great back-to-back games for Keyonte and there might be a sell high window here.

item.title: [Recap] Jayson Tatum (BOS): Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jayson Tatum had 24 points (10-of-23 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), eight rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Wednesday.

Tatum led the Celtics with 24 points Wednesday, but a late technical foul proved costly in the loss to the Nuggets. The 28-year-old forward was assessed a technical foul in the final seconds of the game for throwing the ball in the direction of an official. This allowed Jamal Murray to make the technical free throw and ice the game for the Nuggets by extending the Denver lead to four. The Celtics begin a back-to-back against the Kings and Warriors on the road Saturday.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Jamal Murray (DEN): Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jamal Murray had 21 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, four steals, two blocks and two three-pointers against the Celtics on Wednesday.

Murray was excellent and finished with a complete stat line against the Celtics Wednesday. The 29-year-old guard hit a clutch jumper to put the Nuggets up by three with less than 10 seconds left in regulation. Following a technical foul on Jayson Tatum, Murray then hit a free throw to ice the game. Denver improved to 8-5 on the season while the Celtics fell to 11-4.

Nick Shlain

item.title: [Recap] Domantas Sabonis (SAC): Domantas Sabonis accounted for eight points (4-of-7 FGs), 13 rebounds, eight assists and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Suns.

It’s honestly impressive considering he’s playing with his thumb wrapped up and he was hitting shots in this one. item.title: [Recap] Brandon Miller (CHA): Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Brandon Miller notched 28 points (10-of-19 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and five three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

Fantasy managers have been waiting for Miller to snap out of his shooting slump for quite some time, and he may have done so on Tuesday. The Hornets wing shot over 50 percent from the field, and 28 points was the most he’s scored in a game since October 28 against the Pistons. Miller has been asked to create more looks for himself off the dribble, and it’s been a struggle. Miller is still shooting 35.9 percent from the field, so the buy-low window may not be closed just yet. Also, while he played 32 minutes, the Hornets shut Miller down at the end of regulation, leaving him to watch overtime from the bench.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Naz Reid (CHA): Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.
item.description:
Naz Reid (nose) accounted for 23 points (8-of-18 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 11 rebounds, four assists, two steals, two blocks and four three-pointers in Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers.

The line Reid recorded against the Lakers was in line with what many fantasy managers hoped to see from him consistently in Charlotte. Unfortunately, things haven’t worked out that way, and Tuesday’s overtime loss dropped the Hornets to 4-10. Making matters worse for Reid was an inadvertent elbow from Collin Sexton that he took to the nose late in overtime. He was subbed out and did not return. With Coby White and Brandon Miller shut down at the end of regulation, the Hornets lacked the options needed to potentially force a second overtime.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Coby White (CHA): Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.
item.description:
Coby White finished Tuesday’s loss to the Lakers with 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, three steals and two three-pointers.

Although White has played in each of Charlotte’s last seven games, the team continues to limit his minutes. He logged 26 minutes on Tuesday and, along with Brandon Miller, did not play at all in overtime. The injuries and minutes restrictions the Hornets have dealt with have a lot to do with them being the worst fourth-quarter team in the NBA this season. Down the stretch on Tuesday, White and the other Hornets failed to do much offensively, with even inbounding the ball becoming an adventure. Charlotte doesn’t play again until Friday, which may be a good thing for White.

Raphielle Johnson

item.title: [Recap] Kevon Looney (LAL): Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.
item.description:
Kevon Looney finished Tuesday’s loss to the Hornets with four points (2-of-3 FGs) and seven rebounds.

With Walker Kessler (leg) out, the Lakers turned to Looney to start at center on Tuesday. While the veteran center grabbed seven rebounds, he played only 17 minutes, and his mobility was an issue. With Sandro Mamukelashvili (3/3/2/1) shooting 1-of-8 from the field, Lakers head coach JJ Redick eventually turned to two-way contract player Carson Cooper. While his numbers (3/4/2 in 18 minutes) won’t jump off the page, Cooper’s contributions as a rebounder and defender were one reason why the Lakers were able to rally. Kessler is expected to be available for Wednesday’s game against the Jazz, so Looney may find himself out of the rotation once again.
